value.name: Rosa escorts Asha to the door
value.description: Rosa walks Asha to the threshold as Asha leaves the house after the rain has stopped.
evidence: When she left the house that afternoon, Rosa walked her to the door.
The street smelled of wet brick.

value.name: Rosa warns Asha about Daniel's accusations
value.description: At the doorway, Rosa tells Asha that Daniel will call her bitter and accuse her of wanting something.
evidence: "Ms. Devi," Rosa said quietly, at the threshold. "He will tell you I am bitter. He will tell you I want something.

value.name: Rosa reveals her employment is ending
value.description: Rosa explains that the bank has already told her her position ends with the estate and that she wants nothing more from the house.
evidence: I want you to know before he tells you that I have already been told by the bank that my position ends with the estate. There is nothing more for me to want here.

value.name: Asha acknowledges Rosa's statement
value.description: Asha responds that she understands Rosa's explanation.

value.name: Rosa predicts Asha will understand later
value.description: Rosa gently tells Asha that she does not understand yet but will eventually.
evidence: "I don't think you do yet," Rosa said, not unkindly, "but you will."

value.name: Rosa closes the door
value.description: Rosa ends the conversation by shutting the door.

value.name: Asha reviews conflicting statements
value.description: That night, Asha sits in her Walnut Street office and compares Daniel's and Rosa's accounts in two columns on a legal pad.
evidence: That night Asha sat in her office on Walnut Street with the file open and a cup of tea going cold beside it, and she made herself two columns on a legal pad.
On one side she wrote what Daniel had said. On the other she wrote what Rosa had said.

value.name: Asha notes Lucia's silence
value.description: Asha realizes she cannot yet make a column for Lucia because Lucia has not said enough.
evidence: She did not yet have a column for Lucia, because Lucia had not yet said enough, and that, she thought, was itself worth noting.

value.name: Asha examines the will
value.description: Asha studies Helena Serrano's will and signature while reflecting on the estate plan and the family's changed circumstances over eleven years.
evidence: She looked at Helena Serrano's signature on the last page, a firm round hand.

She thought about a woman who had executed an estate plan eleven years ago when her older son was the responsible one and her younger daughter was a film school student in California, and she thought about what eleven years could do to a household.

value.name: Asha senses hidden tension at the dinner table
value.description: Asha recalls feeling that three people at the dining room table were waiting for the right question while the fourth feared it.
evidence: She thought about what she had felt at the dining room table, which was that three of the four people in that room had been waiting for someone to ask the right question, and the fourth had been afraid she would.
participants: three of the four people in that room
